what: The ownership rule for a task — 'is this mine to act on?' — as a table of cases both languages answer. Rust: cal_core::is_mine_or_unassigned. TypeScript: isMineOrUnassigned in shared/taskAssignment.ts. Both suites read THIS file, so the two cannot drift apart in silence.
why: The rule is not a wire format, it is a DECISION, and both sides make it independently on the same data. Rust makes it when it decides whether a task rings: enumerate_external_triggers drops a colleague's task before a Trigger is ever built. TypeScript makes it when it decides what to offer in the day-start review and how to split 'Done — N by me, M by others'. Neither can see the other's answer. If they disagree, the failure is silent in the worst direction: a phone that rings for a task the app never shows as mine, or a task the app treats as mine that never rings. Nothing crashes, nothing logs, and finding it means noticing over days that one surface disagrees with the other.

shape.note: Each case gives the task's assignee ids and the account's own identity, then the expected answer. Identity is compared by id ALONE — providers return the same person with different display names per endpoint, so matching on name or email would drop a real assignment.
shape.assignees: list of user ids assigned to the task; empty means nobody
shape.me: the account's own user id, or null when the adapter reports no identity at all

cases.name: personal-list-no-identity
cases.note: The local store and other personal-style adapters never report a 'me'. Answering false here would silence every reminder the user has, on the surface where they have the most.

cases.name: no-identity-but-someone-assigned
cases.note: Same, even when assignees arrived from elsewhere: with no identity there is nobody to compare against, so the rule must not guess.

cases.name: unassigned-in-a-shared-list
cases.note: Nobody has taken it, so it is everyone's — including mine. This is what keeps a shared Vikunja project usable before anyone claims anything.

cases.name: assigned-to-me-and-a-colleague
cases.note: Multi-assignee sources (Vikunja) put several people on one task. Being one of them is enough.

cases.name: assigned-only-to-a-colleague
cases.note: THE case the rule exists for, and the only false one. A colleague's task must not ring on my phone, must not be offered in my day-start review, and must not be counted among the things I finished. It stays VISIBLE — this decides ownership, not visibility.
